hbm.channels.justification: HBM channel count.  The two design points state different HBM provisioning: the ROM point buys the stacks its area_fractions.hbm_phy pays for and serves KV alone from them (points[ROM].kv_transfer_bytes_per_step / component_times_s.kv_read), while the GPU point buys 8 stacks per package and serves weights AND KV from one pool (points[GPU].kv_transfer_bytes_per_step / component_times_s.kv_read).  A ROM point whose kv_store is `sram` buys none at all (area_fractions.hbm_phy 0.0) and carries a single inert channel.  Both sides resolve to the SAME hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel; only the channel count differs, which is exactly what the design points say differs.  THIS ANCHOR: Qwen3-8B/ROM-N5-native-HBMKV-array-tensor-x4 (kv_store 'hbm', token_slots 1, 4 devices) against Qwen3-8B/b200_sxm-x2-tensor (kv_store 'hbm', token_slots 1, 2 devices).

rom.arrays.justification: ROM array count.  The ROM design point stores its weights in ROM and the GPU design point has no ROM at all; the HBM machine carries a single inert array because the cost-table schema requires the full parameter set, and no MEMORY_OBJECT in the HBM deployment is stamped StorageClass.ROM, so it is never read.  THIS ANCHOR: Qwen3-8B/ROM-N5-native-HBMKV-array-tensor-x4 (kv_store 'hbm', token_slots 1, 4 devices) against Qwen3-8B/b200_sxm-x2-tensor (kv_store 'hbm', token_slots 1, 2 devices).

rom.bytes_per_cycle_per_array.justification: Per-array ROM read rate.  Derived on the ROM machine from points[ROM].peak_weight_read_bytes_s; inert on the HBM machine.  THIS ANCHOR: Qwen3-8B/ROM-N5-native-HBMKV-array-tensor-x4 (kv_store 'hbm', token_slots 1, 4 devices) against Qwen3-8B/b200_sxm-x2-tensor (kv_store 'hbm', token_slots 1, 2 devices).

rom.interleave_bytes.justification: ROM address stripe, set equal to the burst quantum so consecutive bursts land on consecutive arrays; inert on the HBM machine.  THIS ANCHOR: Qwen3-8B/ROM-N5-native-HBMKV-array-tensor-x4 (kv_store 'hbm', token_slots 1, 4 devices) against Qwen3-8B/b200_sxm-x2-tensor (kv_store 'hbm', token_slots 1, 2 devices).

rom.transaction_bytes.justification: ROM burst quantum, set equal to rom.bytes_per_cycle_per_array so the model's ceil(transaction_bytes / bytes_per_cycle) is exactly 1 and no bandwidth is lost to quantisation; inert on the HBM machine.  THIS ANCHOR: Qwen3-8B/ROM-N5-native-HBMKV-array-tensor-x4 (kv_store 'hbm', token_slots 1, 4 devices) against Qwen3-8B/b200_sxm-x2-tensor (kv_store 'hbm', token_slots 1, 2 devices).

parameters.derivation: 3 sequencer cycles (sequencer.fetch_cycles + decode_cycles + issue_cycles, the cycle model's per-instruction front end) divided by technology.json#latency.sequencer_issue_decode_s = 3e-09 s.  The analytical model states no clock; this is the one analytical quantity that fixes one.  Every rate below is an analytical B/s or ops/s divided by this clock, so a different clock would move the per-cycle numbers and leave every derived TIME unchanged.

The analytical model prices no engine byte-port bandwidth.  Both machines are given the larger of the pair's weight-path rates (4.752960e+14 B/s) so that no simulated time is attributed to an engine port the analytical model does not model.  At the shipped 64 B/cycle this would throttle DMA to 6.400e+10 B/s, 7426x below the ROM array it drains.

technology.json#latency.pipeline_fill_drain_s 3.2e-08 s + one global wire traversal sqrt(reticle.area_mm2) x global_wire_delay_s_per_mm = 4.282231e-09 s, the analytical array-pass boundary 3.628223e-08 s, times the clock = 36.2822 cycles.  The analytical model charges 4 of these per layer; the cycle model charges one per engine instruction and has no per-layer hook, so the difference between the deployment's instructions per layer and 4 is a reported residual, not a tuned parameter.

The narrowest tensor operator output width in Qwen3-8B (1024: attention.key_projection, attention.value_projection), read from build/ir-v3/qwen3-8b/kernel_ir.v3.json over the 253 kernels it declares with counter_class tensor.  At batch 1 the cycle model's tensor rate is min(lanes, tile_cols*issue_window, cols) x work_per_lane_cycle x clock, so lanes above the operator's own output width are masked and deliver nothing.  1024 is the largest lane count for which EVERY tensor operator of this model runs at the full derived roof; at 4096 the MAC-weighted achieved rate falls to 89.3% of the roof; at 12288 the MAC-weighted achieved rate falls to 44.7% of the roof.  The pair (lanes, work_per_lane_cycle) is a gauge split of one analytical quantity -- their product times the clock is what the design point pins -- and this rule fixes the split by exactness.

compute roof / (lanes x clock), in work-counter units.  The roof is the design point's OWN arithmetic over the design point's OWN published time: bf16 15136811008 = 15136811008 operations / component_times_s.compute 5.570312088214652e-05 s = 2.7174080677e+14 ops/s.  That identity is exact by construction, which is the point: a literal 'bf16' index into operations_by_canonical_format raises on a w4a8 design point and a literal 'bf16' compute density prices one 2.7x too slow WITHOUT raising.  Cross-checked against the technology derivation the study built the term from -- sum over formats of ops_f / (area_fractions.compute 0.22290895663237373 x silicon_area_mm2 3260.0 x compute_ops_s_per_mm2[f] x efficiencies.compute 0.55), times token_slots 1 -- which gives 5.570312088214652e-05 s against the published 5.570312088214652e-05 s, agreeing to +0.000e+00 relative.  Units: the cost table declares this parameter in work/lane/cycle and the shipped characterized value was measured as (tensor.multiplications + tensor.additions) / cycles; the analytical operations count is a work count too, at 2 operations per active parameter (the multiply-and-add fallback), so no conversion is needed and none is applied.  That makes the machine's MAC rate lanes x work_per_lane_cycle / 2 x clock = 1.3587040338e+14 MAC/s.  In the cycle model this value divides the K extent (ceil(tile_depth x work_scale / work_per_lane_cycle)), so it is the reduction-tree width of one output lane -- 132.69 MACs deep -- and not a second lane count.

The cycle model builds NO fabric on TopologyClass.SINGLE_CHIP (runtime/cycle/fabric.py:923-930), so a single-chip run has structurally zero link cycles.  points[ROM] charges 72 hop events per token (two all-reduces per layer per token over 4 partitions inside one nvlink5 domain) and points[GPU] 72 (two all-reduces per layer per token over 2 partitions inside one nvlink5 domain).  The derived machines express each anchor as ONE logical device holding the resource one token can engage, which is exactly the transformation that removes the inter-device fabric; the term is therefore absent by construction and is reported, not approximated.  It is 68.2% of the analytical ROM step and 12.1% of the GPU step, so removing it is NOT neutral between the two sides and the reconciliation reports the ratio with the analytical link added back as well as without it.

The five analytical component times do NOT sum to the analytical step.  step = max(memory_time, compute_time) / efficiencies.stage_balance + link_latency + layer_fixed_latency, with memory_time = weight + kv when the design point shares one memory path and max(weight, kv) when it does not (points[ROM].overlap_rule 'weights and KV are physically separate arrays: their times overlap').  token_slots does NOT appear as a separate factor here because the published component times ALREADY carry it (src/opentallas/roofline.py:3288-3297): they are the per-slot cost times the slots a token traverses.  This anchor is token_slots 1 on the ROM side and 1 on the GPU side.  stage_balance 0.9 is applied where devices > 1 and the parallelism is not none, which is the case on both sides here; collapsing each point to one logical device sets devices = 1, so the derived machines do not carry it and it is reported.

A token traverses 1 slot(s) on the ROM design and 1 on the GPU design, and can engage only one at a time.  The collapsed logical device therefore carries the design's AGGREGATE resource DIVIDED BY ITS OWN SLOT COUNT -- ROM weight 4.753021e+14 / 1 = 4.753021e+14 B/s, GPU memory 1.440000e+13 / 1 = 1.440000e+13 B/s -- which is what reproduces each side's published PER-TOKEN term.  Carrying the undivided aggregate on both sides instead would remove a factor of 1 from one machine and 1 from the other, handing the more deeply pipelined side a 1x speed-up the study never granted it.  That is the class of defect this generator exists to prevent, so it is not done.  What the collapse DOES remove is the pipeline's aggregate throughput view: the derived machines model one token's latency, not the design's 3911.3 aggregate tokens/s.

The two models do not agree on the total arithmetic.  The analytical count for this model is the explicit active-parameter fallback, active_parameters 7568405504 x 2, with NO attention arithmetic and no context dependence.  The cycle model counts attention separately (attention.score_multiplications, attention.value_multiplications), which at context 8192 is 2.416e+09 extra MACs per token.  The models agree on the weight-driven multiply count and disagree on the total; this is structural and cannot be tuned away.

The shared arithmetic roof is taken from the ROM point ALONE, which is what a single derivation means and what makes every compute parameter identical on the two machines.  The GPU point prices its own arithmetic at a published per-part roof, not at area x density: 1.513681e+10 operations over component_times_s.compute 6.115883235555556e-06 s = 2.475000e+15 ops/s, 9.108x the shared roof 2.717408e+14 ops/s.  The derived GPU machine therefore CANNOT reproduce its own analytical compute term, and the direction is NOT the same in every cell: here the shared roof is BELOW the GPU point's own, so the derived GPU machine is HANDICAPPED by 9.108x.  It is reported rather than corrected because correcting it would mean two compute roofs, which is the defect this generator exists to prevent.  Whether it matters is checkable: the GPU point is memory-bound by 171.9x on the analytical side, against a compute factor of 9.108x, which leaves it still memory-bound.

The analytical ROM weight_read term is a full sweep of the STORED array: stored_weight_bytes 16381470720 / peak_weight_read_bytes_s x token_slots 1 = 3.446539e-05 s per slot pass.  The cycle model has no full-sweep semantics: it charges only the bytes the deployment's accesses touch, and at batch 1 the weight amplification is 1, so it will charge engaged_weight_bytes 15136811008 (92.40% of stored).  On a sparse MoE point that fraction is small and the divergence is the dominant one on this term.  The reconciliation must compare the cycle model's ROM traffic against the engaged bytes and report the sweep-versus-touched difference as a modelling divergence, not a machine parameter.

rom.interleave_bytes and rom.transaction_bytes are both set to rom.bytes_per_cycle_per_array, so one full stripe across the array pool is 16 x 29706 = 475296 bytes.  runtime/cycle/model.py:1302 stripes on address // interleave_bytes and :1336 charges ceil(bytes / transaction_bytes) transactions, so a ROM access SMALLER than 475296 bytes engages only some of the arrays and any access below one transaction costs exactly one cycle whatever its size.  Nothing in this tool checks the emitted stripe against a deployment's actual ROM access sizes, and the stripe scales with the model: it is a machine-side granularity assumption, not an analytical value, and a run whose ROM reads are smaller than the stripe will not see the derived aggregate rate.

The analytical term is 1.894112e-07 s per layer built from four primitives; only the array-pass boundary has a cycle-model counterpart, and the cycle model charges it per engine INSTRUCTION, not per layer.  The layer barrier (3.5e-08 s per layer, 1.260 us per token) has no counterpart on a single chip at all.
